terms.gloss: a defence; the speech or case for the accused
evidence: Cic. Cael. 4: ad istam omnem ōrātiōnem brevis est dēfēnsiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also any defending: of a town (Caes. B.G. 2.7), of a friend’s standing (Cic. Fam. 1.7.2).

terms.gloss: to answer a charge, make one’s defence
terms.grammar: phrase: causa, causae f. with dīcō, dīcere, dīxī, dictum
terms.comment: Said of the accused defending himself, and of the advocate pleading for him (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.8: inter sīcāriōs dēfendere (Lewis & Short, s.v. sīcārius)
Traupman 194: causam alicūjus dēfendere, defend someone
terms.comment: The general verb for defending and protecting (see protect). In court, of the advocate: inter sīcāriōs dēfendere, to defend on a charge of murder.

phrases.latin: ad istam omnem ōrātiōnem brevis est dēfēnsiō.
phrases.english: to all that speech of yours the defence is short.

sources: Lewis & Short: defensio · Lewis & Short: causa · Lewis & Short: defendo · Lewis & Short: sicarius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 194, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
